newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela work stoppage has widespread support.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela work stoppage has widespread support.

text.p: A planned 12-hour work stoppage called by Venezuela's largest union, won the backing Monday of parties across the political spectrum and even the government itself.

The Venezuelan Workers Confederation (CTV) has announced the August 6 national work stoppage to protest against a 27 percent rise in gasoline prices, rising public services costs and the failure of private sector companies to raise wages.

The strike call has been encouraged by top government officials with Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar describing it as "justified" and Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff calling it "a legitimate means of pressure".
Political parties, both government-backing and opposition, added their support for the unions Monday.

The high cost of living and poor standard of public services, "are good reasons for workers to radicalize their means of struggle," said Aristedes Hospedales, spokesman for Democratic Action (AD), Venezuela's largest political party.
AD is closely tied to the CTV with most CTV leaders being AD members.
Opposition party social Christian Copei also backed the strike, which it said was a message to the government.
"The work stoppage is a popular judgment against the government," Copei General Secretary Donald Ramirez told reporters.
Ramirez said it was ridiculous for the government to back the strike, "when it is the product of its misguided policies."

Government-backing Movement to Socialism (MAS) said the strike was a legitimate means to ensure that private businesses met their commitment to raise salaries and urged the government to take action if the strike was ignored.
"We support all actions to demand that this commitment be met and if it is not, we believe the government should intervene," said MAS vice-President Freddy Diaz.
Government officials have suggested that salaries could be raised by decree if businesses do not increase them voluntarily.
